languages.name: AppSec
languages.notes: OWASP Top 10 / ASVS / CWE-aligned secure SDLC

libraries.name: bandit
libraries.purpose: Security linter that finds common security issues in Python via AST plugin checks: hardcoded passwords, eval/exec, weak hashes (MD5/SHA1), disabled TLS verification, SQL built by string concatenation. Use as a cheap first-pass CI gate, not a substitute for taint-tracking SAST.

libraries.name: semgrep
libraries.purpose: Fast semantic 'grep for code' SAST across 30+ languages using pattern/taint rules that look like the code; runs in IDE, pre-commit, and CI. CE is local-first (code not uploaded by default, intra-file); cross-file/dataflow needs AppSec Platform.

libraries.name: gitleaks
libraries.purpose: Detect hardcoded secrets (API keys, tokens, passwords) in git repos, files, and stdin via regex + entropy; deploy as pre-commit hook and CI gate with SARIF output. Feature-complete; maintainer shifting focus to Betterleaks.

libraries.name: trivy
libraries.purpose: Comprehensive scanner for vulnerabilities (CVEs) in OS packages, app dependencies, container images, IaC misconfig, secrets, and SBOM (CycloneDX/SPDX). Self-hostable; covers multi-ecosystem dependency scanning.

libraries.name: dependency-check
libraries.purpose: OWASP SCA utility that detects known, publicly disclosed vulnerabilities in dependencies via CPE fuzzy matching against NVD; needs an NVD API key for reasonable update speed. Maven/Gradle/CLI.

libraries.name: detect-secrets
libraries.purpose: Yelp's tool to detect and prevent committing secrets; uses a baseline of known secrets so only new leaks fail, integrates with pre-commit and pre-receive hooks. Pairs with gitleaks.

libraries.name: cryptography
libraries.purpose: PyCA's high-level wrapper around OpenSSL providing safe primitives (Fernet, AES-GCM, RSA, ECC, SHA-3). Prefer over hand-rolled crypto; use AEAD and avoid MD5/SHA1 for security.

libraries.name: pynacl
libraries.purpose: Python binding to libsodium; misuse-resistant high-level boxes: SecretBox (symmetric), Box/SealedBox (public-key, Curve25519), SigningKey (Ed25519), pwhash (Argon2id). Use for app-level crypto instead of assembling primitives.

libraries.name: libsodium
libraries.purpose: Modern, portable, misuse-resistant crypto library (NaCl fork): crypto_secretbox, crypto_box, crypto_sign, crypto_pwhash (Argon2id), crypto_kdf. Opinionated safe defaults; call sodium_init() once. Not for TLS (use OpenSSL/BoringSSL).

libraries.name: vault
libraries.purpose: HashiCorp Vault: centralized secrets management with dynamic, short-lived, leased credentials; encryption-as-a-service, rotation, and fine-grained access policies. Inject at runtime, never in source or client bundles.

libraries.name: codeql
libraries.purpose: GitHub's query-based semantic code analysis (QL) for data-flow/taint analysis across many languages; powers GitHub code scanning. Free for open-source/research; commercial license needed for closed-source CI. Strong for source-sink reasoning.

patterns.title: Least-privilege credentials & runtime injection
patterns.problem: Hardcoded admin keys in repos/client bundles; over-broad OAuth/API scopes; secrets in .env committed to git (A02/A05).
patterns.solution: Centralize secrets in a manager (Vault/AWS Secrets Manager/Key Vault); inject at runtime; use OIDC federation with short-lived tokens in CI/CD; scope tokens per feature; rotate with staging labels.
patterns.anti_pattern: Embedding API keys in source or frontend bundles; using one long-lived admin token for everything.
patterns.snippet:
# CI: exchange OIDC for short-lived token, never store cloud keys
# export $(vault read -field=token secret/ci/role)

patterns.title: Parameterized queries & strict input validation
patterns.problem: String-concatenated SQL, shell, OS commands, and HTML allow injection (CWE-89, CWE-78, CWE-79).
patterns.solution: Use parameterized/prepared statements and ORM query builders; allowlist input validation; output-encode per context; never build queries by concatenation.
patterns.anti_pattern: cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM u WHERE id=' + user_id) or subprocess(shell=True) with user input.

patterns.title: Continuous dependency vulnerability scanning (SCA)
patterns.problem: Transitive dependencies with known CVEs ship to production (A06:2021 Vulnerable and Outdated Components).
patterns.solution: Run ecosystem-native audits (pip-audit, npm audit) plus Trivy/Dependency-Check/OSV-Scanner in CI on every PR; fail on HIGH/CRITICAL; enable Dependabot/Renovate for fix PRs.
patterns.anti_pattern: Manual, occasional checks; ignoring transitive deps; pinning without monitoring advisories.

patterns.title: Use AEAD & misuse-resistant crypto libraries
patterns.problem: Hand-rolled crypto, ECB mode, MD5/SHA1, hardcoded keys, and nonce reuse leak plaintext or weaken integrity.
patterns.solution: Use libsodium/PyNaCl or the cryptography lib with AEAD (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305); Argon2id for password hashing; generate random 32-byte keys; never reuse a nonce with the same key.
patterns.anti_pattern: DES/3DES, MD5 password hashes, AES in ECB mode, reusing IVs/nonces.
patterns.snippet:
from cryptography.fernet import Fernet
token = Fernet(key).encrypt(data)

patterns.title: Pre-commit + CI secrets gate with baseline
patterns.problem: Secrets committed to git persist in history and are scraped by attackers.
patterns.solution: Run gitleaks/detect-secrets as pre-commit and CI; maintain a baseline so only NEW secrets fail; on leak, rotate immediately and purge history with git filter-repo.
patterns.anti_pattern: Relying on code review alone; using SKIP=gitleaks to bypass; deleting only from HEAD.
patterns.snippet: gitleaks git --pre-commit --staged   # or detect-secrets pre-commit hook

patterns.title: Shift-left security & threat modeling
patterns.problem: 'We'll add security later' leads to baked-in hardcoding, disabled TLS validation, and misconfig (per r/AskNetsec dev-culture threads).
patterns.solution: Bake OWASP Proactive Controls into the SDLC; threat-model in design; add SAST/SCA gates in CI from day one; treat dev/test like prod.
patterns.anti_pattern: Deferring all security to a post-launch 'security sprint'; disabling TLS validation by default.

patterns.title: Least privilege & explicit authorization (A01)
patterns.problem: Missing/incorrect authorization (CWE-862/863), IDOR, and over-privileged services (A01:2021 Broken Access Control).
patterns.solution: Deny-by-default authorization at every operation; verify object ownership server-side; scope service identities; apply OWASP ASVS V4/V8.
patterns.anti_pattern: Trusting client-supplied role/tenant IDs; checking authz only at the UI layer.

patterns.title: Security logging & monitoring (A09)
patterns.problem: Insufficient logging/monitoring lets breaches go undetected; logs can leak secrets/PII.
patterns.solution: Log authn/authz decisions, redact tokens/PII, centralize with alerting and tamper-protection; meet OWASP ASVS V7.
patterns.anti_pattern: Logging full request bodies with credentials; no alerting on repeated 401/403.

patterns.title: SSRF protection for outbound requests (A10)
patterns.problem: Server-side request forgery lets attackers reach internal services via user-supplied URLs.
patterns.solution: Allowlist destinations; block link-local/metadata (169.254.169.254); validate then re-resolve; disable unused URL schemes.
patterns.anti_pattern: Fetching arbitrary user URLs with server credentials attached.

methodologies.name: OWASP Top 10 Proactive Controls
methodologies.summary: OWASP's prioritized list of the top 10 controls every developer should implement (C1-C10): parameterize queries, encode/escape, validate, authn/authz, crypto, error handling, logging, data protection, security config, SCA.
methodologies.steps:
C1 Define security requirements
C2 Leverage security frameworks & libraries
C3 Secure database access (parameterize)
C4 Encode/escape input
C5 Validate input
C6 Implement digital identity
C7 Enforce access controls
C8 Protect data everywhere
C9 Implement security logging/monitoring
C10 Handle all errors/exceptions securely

methodologies.name: Secure SDLC / Shift-Left
methodologies.summary: Integrate security into every phase: threat model in design, SAST+SCA+secret scans in CI, secure code review, and DAST before release.
methodologies.steps:
1. Requirements: map OWASP ASVS / legal
2. Design: threat model (STRIDE / abuse cases)
3. Build: SAST (bandit/semgrep) + secret scan (gitleaks) pre-commit/CI
4. Dependencies: SCA (Trivy/Dependency-Check) per PR
5. Test: secure code review + DAST
6. Release/Operate: logging, monitoring, patch cadence

methodologies.name: Threat Modeling (STRIDE)
methodologies.summary: Structured identification of threats per component: Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, Elevation of privilege.
methodologies.steps:
1. Diagram system / data flows (DFD)
2. Decompose using STRIDE per element
3. Identify threats and root causes
4. Rate risk (likelihood x impact)
5. Define mitigations mapped to CWE/ASVS
6. Validate and track to closure

methodologies.name: Secrets Management Lifecycle
methodologies.summary: Centralize, inject at runtime, shorten TTL, and audit. Pair detect-prevent (pre-commit/CI) with rotation and history purge on leak.
methodologies.steps:
1. Inventory all secrets & where used
2. Move to a manager (Vault/AWS SM/Key Vault)
3. Inject at runtime; OIDC short-lived tokens in CI
4. Least-privilege scopes per feature
5. Automated rotation with staging labels
6. On leak: rotate + git filter-repo purge + alert

methodologies.name: OWASP SAMM (DevSecOps Maturity)
methodologies.summary: Software Assurance Maturity Model: measure and roadmap secure-development maturity across governance, design, implementation, verification, operations.
methodologies.steps:
1. Assess current maturity per SAMM stream
2. Set target levels with stakeholders
3. Implement pipeline gates (SAST/SCA/secret scan)
4. Train devs on Proactive Controls
5. Measure progress; iterate roadmap
6. Independent verification (ASVS level)
